messages.content:
Return only the shortest standalone answer that preserves every unique fact. No heading, label, preamble, recap or explanation of what the reader should infer. Combine related facts into complete sentences; mention each fact once. Attach evidence IDs in parentheses. Prefer specific verbs and short clauses. Remove redundant implications, repeated subjects and conversational framing. Aim for 35–45 words for verbose material; meaning wins if more are essential.

Preserve every result, condition, exclusion, uncertainty, owner and next action. Preserve exact numbers, units, names, field names, paths, commands, errors, frontmatter and code blocks. Do not claim an instruction happened or an untested result passed. Check all source facts silently before answering.

Already concise: copy EXACTLY. Requested JSON: exact keys/types, no surrounding text. Explicitly requested detail: retain ordered steps, reasons and provenance.

Existing memo edits require requested preview and approved revision-checked memo.write. Stop on conflicts; preserve source evidence. Use one normal drafting call.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: memo.
Write a standalone incident handoff.

Source:
The incident record concerns the preview service rather than the main application. Between 10:05 and 10:12 UTC, preview requests returned HTTP 503. The main application continued serving requests during that interval. Investigation found that the preview process could not acquire its local lock. The log contained the exact message "preview lock unavailable". We have not established who held that lock, so the handoff must not name an owner as though that were known. Restarting the preview process restored previews at 10:12 UTC. That is the observed recovery, not evidence that the lock ownership question has been solved. The supporting log is incident-preview-8. The next step belongs to Oren, who will add lock-owner diagnostics and reproduce the contention in a disposable fixture. The purpose of this handoff is to allow someone who did not see the incident discussion to understand the affected surface, the recovery and the remaining investigation.

message.content: Incident handoff: preview service returned HTTP 503 from 10:05 to 10:12 UTC; the main application was unaffected. The preview process could not acquire its local lock; the log contained "preview lock unavailable". Lock ownership is unknown. Restarting the preview process restored service at 10:12 UTC, but this does not resolve the lock question. Supporting log: incident-preview-8. Next step: Oren will add lock-owner diagnostics and reproduce contention in a disposable fixture.
